title: When people first reached Australia
summary: Most scholars place first arrival between about 50,000 and 65,000 years ago. The 65,000-year date from Madjedbebe has been challenged, and a conservative minimum is about 48,000 years.
why: It anchors the deep history of Aboriginal Australians and of human spread out of Africa.
question: When did the first people arrive in Australia?
evidence: Madjedbebe rock shelter dated about 65,000 years; a 2020 study argued that dating is unreliable; genomic estimates point to roughly 43,000–60,000 years ago.
wouldSettle: Independent dating methods agreeing on undisturbed human layers at Madjedbebe or another early site.

theories.name: Early arrival, about 65,000 years
theories.idea: Madjedbebe's artefacts show people were in northern Australia about 65,000 years ago.

theories.name: Later arrival, about 50,000 years
theories.idea: Dating problems mean the secure minimum is about 48,000–50,000 years, matching genomic estimates.
